symbols.doc:
Shared base for `cherry-pick` and `revert`: the same commit list, the same
`--no-commit`/`--mainline`, and the same four control flags. Only the
subcommand's name and the extra flags differ, which is why they are one
implementation rather than two that drift.

members.name: commits
members.doc: The commits to replay (positional, required); repeatable.

members.name: noCommit
members.doc: Apply the change without committing it (`-n`/`--no-commit`).

members.name: mainline
members.doc:
Which parent of a merge commit to treat as the mainline
(`-m <parent-number>`), counting from 1. Replaying a merge needs it: git
cannot otherwise tell which side of the merge the change is.

members.name: signoff
members.doc: Add a `Signed-off-by` trailer (`--signoff`).

members.name: skip
members.doc: Drop the current commit and carry on (`--skip`).

symbols.name: GitResetSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `git reset`.

members.name: ref
members.doc: The commit to reset to (positional); defaults to `HEAD`.

members.name: paths
members.doc: Reset only these pathspecs — unstaging them (positional); repeatable.

members.name: soft
members.doc: Move the branch only, keeping the index and working tree (`--soft`).

members.name: mixed
members.doc: Reset the index but not the working tree (`--mixed`), git's default.

members.name: hard
members.doc: Reset the index *and* the working tree (`--hard`), discarding changes.

members.name: merge
members.doc: Reset, keeping changes to files that differ between the commits (`--merge`).

members.name: keep
members.doc: Like {@link merge}, but refuse when a changed file differs (`--keep`).

symbols.name: GitRestoreSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `git restore`.

members.name: paths
members.doc: The pathspecs to restore (positional, required); repeatable.

members.name: source
members.doc:
Restore the contents from this commit or tree (`--source=<tree-ish>`)
rather than from the index.

members.name: staged
members.doc:
Restore the index (`--staged`) — unstaging the paths. Combine with
{@link worktree} to reset both, which is what `git restore -SW` does.

members.name: worktree
members.doc: Restore the working tree (`--worktree`), git's default when neither is given.

symbols.name: GitRevertSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `git revert`.

members.name: noEdit
members.doc: Take the generated message without opening an editor (`--no-edit`).

symbols.name: GitRevListSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `git rev-list`.

members.name: count
members.doc:
Print how many commits the walk found rather than listing them
(`--count`). Prefer {@link "./git.ts".GitTasks.commitCount}, which reads
that number back.

members.name: maxCount
members.doc: Stop after this many commits (`--max-count=<n>`).

members.name: skip
members.doc: Skip this many commits before printing (`--skip=<n>`).

members.name: all
members.doc: Walk every ref in `refs/` (`--all`).

members.name: branches
members.doc: Walk every branch (`--branches`).

members.name: tags
members.doc: Walk every tag (`--tags`).

members.name: remotes
members.doc: Walk every remote-tracking branch (`--remotes`).

members.name: noMerges
members.doc: Omit merge commits (`--no-merges`).

members.name: merges
members.doc: Keep only merge commits (`--merges`).

members.name: firstParent
members.doc: Follow only the first parent of each merge (`--first-parent`).

members.name: reverse
members.doc: Emit the commits oldest first (`--reverse`).

members.name: topoOrder
members.doc: Order by topology rather than date (`--topo-order`).

members.name: dateOrder
members.doc: Order by commit date (`--date-order`).

members.name: since
members.doc: Only commits after this date (`--since=<date>`).

members.name: until
members.doc: Only commits before this date (`--until=<date>`).

members.name: author
members.doc: Only commits whose author matches (`--author=<pattern>`).

members.name: commits
members.doc:
The commits or ranges to walk (positional), e.g. `"HEAD"` or
`"origin/main..HEAD"`; repeatable.

members.name: paths
members.doc: Limit the walk to commits touching these paths (positional); repeatable.

symbols.name: GitRevParseSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `git rev-parse`.

members.name: rev
members.doc: The revisions or arguments to resolve (positional); repeatable.

members.name: short
members.doc:
Abbreviate the SHA (`--short`, or `--short=<n>` with a length). git picks
a length long enough to stay unambiguous when none is given.

members.name: abbrevRef
members.doc: Print the ref's short name (`--abbrev-ref`), e.g. `main` for `HEAD`.

members.name: verify
members.doc: Fail rather than echo the argument when it names no object (`--verify`).

members.name: gitDir
members.doc: Print the path of the `.git` directory (`--git-dir`).

members.name: showToplevel
members.doc: Print the absolute path of the working tree's root (`--show-toplevel`).

members.name: showPrefix
members.doc: Print the current directory's path relative to that root (`--show-prefix`).

members.name: isInsideWorkTree
members.doc: Print whether this is inside a working tree (`--is-inside-work-tree`).

symbols.name: GitRmSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `git rm`.

members.name: paths
members.doc: Paths/pathspecs to remove (positional, required); repeatable.

members.name: cached
members.doc:
Remove from the index only, leaving the file on disk (`--cached`) — how a
file committed by mistake stops being tracked without being deleted.

members.name: recursive
members.doc: Recurse into directories (`-r`).

members.name: force
members.doc: Remove even when the file has staged or local changes (`-f`/`--force`).

members.name: dryRun
members.doc: Report what would be removed without removing it (`-n`/`--dry-run`).

members.name: ignoreUnmatch
members.doc: Exit 0 when no path matches (`--ignore-unmatch`).

symbols.name: GitRunner
symbols.doc:
Runs a `git` subcommand and resolves to its trimmed stdout, or `null` when
the command fails (non-zero exit, or `git` unavailable).

symbols.name: GitRunSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for an arbitrary `git` command not covered by a typed task.

members.name: command
members.doc: The subcommand and its arguments, e.g. `command("bisect", "start")`.

symbols.name: GitSequencerSettings
symbols.doc:
Base for the commands that can be left in progress by a conflict. Subclasses
expose only the actions their command accepts — `merge` has no `--skip` —
and call {@link GitSequencerSettings.sequencer_} to record one.

members.name: continue
members.doc: Resume the operation once the conflict is resolved (`--continue`).

members.name: abort
members.doc: Undo it and restore the pre-operation state (`--abort`).

members.name: quit
members.doc: Forget the operation, leaving the tree as it is (`--quit`).

symbols.name: GitSettings
symbols.doc: Shared base for every `git` subcommand: the binary and global options.

members.name: dir
members.doc: Run git as if started in `path` (`-C <path>`).

members.name: config
members.doc: Set a one-off config value (`-c key=value`); repeatable.

symbols.name: GitShortlogEntry
symbols.doc: One line of `git shortlog -s`: a contributor and how many commits they have.

members.name: count
members.doc: How many commits the group holds.

members.name: name
members.doc: The contributor's name, as recorded on the commits.

members.name: email
members.doc: Their email address; present only when `-e` asked for it.

symbols.name: GitShortlogSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `git shortlog`.

members.name: summary
members.doc:
Report only the commit count per author, without the subjects (`-s`).
Prefer {@link "./git.ts".GitTasks.shortlogEntries}, which reads that
output back.

members.name: numbered
members.doc: Sort by commit count rather than by name (`-n`).

members.name: email
members.doc: Include each author's email address (`-e`).

members.name: committer
members.doc: Group by committer rather than author (`-c`).

members.name: group
members.doc: Group by a named field (`--group=<field>`), e.g. `"trailer:co-authored-by"`.

members.name: commits
members.doc: The revision range to summarise (positional); repeatable.

members.name: paths
members.doc: Limit the summary to commits touching these paths (positional).

symbols.name: GitShowRefSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `git show-ref`.

members.name: tags
members.doc: Only tags (`--tags`); may be combined with {@link heads}.

members.name: heads
members.doc: Only branch heads (`--heads`); may be combined with {@link tags}.

members.name: head
members.doc: Include `HEAD` even when a filter would exclude it (`--head`).

members.name: dereference
members.doc: Dereference tags into the objects they point at (`--dereference`).

members.name: hash
members.doc: Print only the object name, without the ref (`--hash`).

members.name: verify
members.doc: Require an exact ref path and fail otherwise (`--verify`).

members.name: exists
members.doc: Check a ref exists without resolving it (`--exists`).

members.name: quietOutput
members.doc:
Suppress git's own stdout (`--quiet`), leaving the exit status as the
answer — the useful pairing with {@link verify}.

Named apart from the inherited `quiet`, which silences Zuke's echo of the
command rather than git's output.

members.name: abbrev
members.doc: Abbreviate object names to this many digits (`--abbrev=<n>`).

members.name: patterns
members.doc: The ref patterns to show (positional); repeatable.

symbols.name: GitShowSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `git show`.

members.name: object
members.doc:
The objects to show (positional); repeatable. A commit, a tag, or a blob
at a revision such as `HEAD:deno.json` — the way a build reads a file as
it was, without checking anything out.

members.name: paths
members.doc: Limit the output to these pathspecs (positional, after `--`); repeatable.

members.name: format
members.doc: Render the commit header through a format string (`--format=<fmt>`).

members.name: noPatch
members.doc: Suppress the diff (`--no-patch`), leaving only the header.

members.name: nameOnly
members.doc: List the changed paths instead of the diff (`--name-only`).

members.name: nameStatus
members.doc: List the changed paths with their status letters (`--name-status`).

members.name: stat
members.doc: Summarise the changes (`--stat`).

symbols.name: GitStashSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `git stash`. Pick the subcommand with {@link push},
{@link pop}, {@link apply}, {@link list}, {@link show}, {@link drop}, or
{@link clear}; the remaining methods apply to the one picked.

members.name: push
members.doc: Stash the working tree and index (`git stash push`).

members.name: pop
members.doc: Restore a stash and drop it (`git stash pop`).

members.name: apply
members.doc: Restore a stash and keep it (`git stash apply`).

members.name: list
members.doc: List the stashes (`git stash list`).

members.name: show
members.doc: Show a stash's diff (`git stash show`).

members.name: drop
members.doc: Discard a stash (`git stash drop`).

members.name: clear
members.doc: Discard every stash (`git stash clear`).

members.name: stash
members.doc:
Which stash to act on, e.g. `stash@{1}` (positional); defaults to the most
recent. Only meaningful for {@link pop}, {@link apply}, {@link show}, and
{@link drop}.

members.name: message
members.doc: Label the stash being pushed (`-m`).

members.name: includeUntracked
members.doc: Stash untracked files too (`--include-untracked`).

members.name: keepIndex
members.doc: Leave what is already staged in the index (`--keep-index`).

members.name: staged
members.doc: Stash only what is staged (`--staged`).

members.name: paths
members.doc: Stash only these pathspecs (positional, after `--`); repeatable.

symbols.name: GitStatusEntry
symbols.doc: One record of `git status --porcelain -z`: a path and how it changed.

members.name: index
members.doc:
The index (staged) status code — git's `X` column: `M` modified, `A`
added, `D` deleted, `R` renamed, `C` copied, `?` untracked, `!` ignored,
or a space when the index matches `HEAD`.

members.name: workingTree
members.doc:
The working-tree status code — git's `Y` column, with the same letters,
or a space when the working tree matches the index.

members.name: path
members.doc: The path, relative to the repository root; for a rename, the new one.

members.name: originalPath
members.doc: Where a renamed or copied entry came from; absent otherwise.

symbols.name: GitStatusSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `git status`.

members.name: short
members.doc: Short-format output (`-s`/`--short`).

members.name: porcelain
members.doc: Stable machine-readable output (`--porcelain`).

members.name: branch
members.doc: Show branch information (`-b`/`--branch`).

members.name: nulTerminated
members.doc:
Terminate each record with a NUL rather than a newline (`-z`), which also
turns on `--porcelain` and stops git quoting unusual paths.

members.name: untrackedFiles
members.doc:
How much of an untracked directory to report (`--untracked-files=<mode>`):
`no`, `normal` (the default — the directory), or `all` (every file in it).

members.name: ignored
members.doc: Also report ignored files (`--ignored`).

members.name: paths
members.doc: Limit the report to these pathspecs (positional); repeatable.

symbols.name: GitSubmoduleSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `git submodule`. Pick the subcommand with {@link add},
{@link init}, {@link deinit}, {@link update}, {@link sync}, {@link status},
or {@link foreach}.

members.name: add
members.doc: Add a submodule (`git submodule add <url> [<path>]`).

members.name: init
members.doc: Register the submodules in `.gitmodules` (`git submodule init`).

members.name: deinit
members.doc: Unregister submodules (`git submodule deinit`).

members.name: update
members.doc: Check the submodules out at their recorded commits (`git submodule update`).

members.name: sync
members.doc: Copy the configured URLs into `.git/config` (`git submodule sync`).

members.name: status
members.doc: Report each submodule's checked-out commit (`git submodule status`).

members.name: foreach
members.doc: Run a command in each submodule (`git submodule foreach <command>`).

members.name: paths
members.doc: Limit the operation to these paths (positional); repeatable.

members.name: withInit
members.doc:
Initialise uninitialised submodules first (`--init`), the flag
{@link update} needs on a fresh clone. Named for the flag rather than the
`init` subcommand, which is what {@link init} runs.

members.name: recursive
members.doc: Recurse into nested submodules (`--recursive`).

members.name: remote
members.doc: Use the upstream branch's latest commit rather than the recorded one (`--remote`).

members.name: force
members.doc: Discard local changes in the submodule (`--force`).

members.name: depth
members.doc: Clone the submodules shallowly (`--depth <n>`).

members.name: jobs
members.doc: Clone this many submodules in parallel (`--jobs <n>`).

members.name: branch
members.doc: Track this branch when adding or updating (`-b <branch>`).

symbols.name: GitSwitchSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `git switch`.

members.name: branch
members.doc: The branch to switch to — or, with {@link create}, the one to create.

members.name: startPoint
members.doc:
The commit the new branch forks from (git's trailing `<start-point>`),
e.g. `origin/main`. Without it a created branch forks from the current
`HEAD`, which is whatever the checkout happened to be on.

members.name: create
members.doc: Create the branch (`-c`); fails if it already exists.

members.name: forceCreate
members.doc: Create the branch, resetting it if it exists (`-C`).

members.name: track
members.doc: Set up upstream tracking (`--track=<mode>`), `direct` or `inherit`.

members.name: detach
members.doc:
Switch with a detached `HEAD` (`--detach`) — checking out a commit rather
than a branch, which `switch` otherwise refuses.

members.name: force
members.doc: Throw away local changes rather than refusing to switch (`--force`).

symbols.name: GitSymbolicRefSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `git symbolic-ref`.

members.name: name
members.doc: The symbolic ref to read or set (positional), e.g. `"HEAD"`.

members.name: ref
members.doc: The ref to point it at (positional), which makes this a write.

members.name: short
members.doc: Shorten the reported ref name (`--short`).

members.name: delete
members.doc: Delete the symbolic ref (`--delete`).

members.name: quietOutput
members.doc:
Say nothing and exit non-zero when the ref is not symbolic (`--quiet`).

Named apart from the inherited `quiet`, which silences Zuke's echo.

members.name: reason
members.doc: The reflog reason to record for the update (`-m <reason>`).

symbols.name: GitTagSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `git tag`.

members.name: name
members.doc: The tag name.

members.name: commit
members.doc:
The commit to tag (git's trailing `<commit>`), rather than `HEAD`. Only
meaningful when creating a tag.

members.name: message
members.doc: Create an annotated tag with this message (`-a -m`).

members.name: force
members.doc: Replace an existing tag (`-f`/`--force`).

members.name: deleteTag
members.doc: Delete the tag (`-d`/`--delete`).

members.name: list
members.doc:
List tags (`-l`), optionally matching a shell pattern such as `v1.*`.
With no pattern, lists them all.

members.name: sort
members.doc:
Order a listing (`--sort=<key>`), e.g. `-v:refname` for newest-version
first — the ordering a release target wants, since the default is
lexicographic and puts `v1.10.0` before `v1.9.0`.

symbols.name: GitTasks
symbols.doc: Typed task functions for the `git` commands.

symbols.name: GitTasksApi
symbols.doc: The shape of {@link GitTasks}.

members.name: init
members.doc: Create a repository: `git init`.

members.name: clone
members.doc: Clone a repository: `git clone`.

members.name: add
members.doc: Stage changes: `git add`.

members.name: rm
members.doc: Remove tracked files: `git rm`.

members.name: mv
members.doc: Move or rename a tracked file: `git mv`.

members.name: restore
members.doc: Restore working-tree or index contents: `git restore`.

members.name: clean
members.doc: Delete untracked files: `git clean`.

members.name: commit
members.doc: Record changes: `git commit`.

members.name: status
members.doc: Show working-tree status: `git status`.

members.name: statusEntries
members.doc:
The working tree's changes as parsed {@link GitStatusEntry} values, from
`git status --porcelain -z` — the form no path can corrupt. An empty array
means a clean tree.

The lambda configures the rest (`.dir()`, `.untrackedFiles()`, `.paths()`);
the output format is fixed, since the parse depends on it.

members.name: checkout
members.doc: Switch branches or restore files: `git checkout`.

members.name: switch
members.doc: Switch branches: `git switch`, `checkout`'s modern half.

members.name: branch
members.doc: Manage branches: `git branch`.

members.name: tag
members.doc: Manage tags: `git tag`.

members.name: push
members.doc: Update remote refs: `git push`.

members.name: pull
members.doc: Fetch and integrate: `git pull`.

members.name: fetch
members.doc: Download objects and refs: `git fetch`.

members.name: remote
members.doc: Manage remotes: `git remote add|remove|rename|set-url|get-url|show|prune`.

members.name: remoteList
members.doc:
The configured remotes as parsed {@link GitRemote} entries, each with the
fetch and push URL folded together, from `git remote --verbose`.

members.name: lsRemote
members.doc: List a remote's refs without fetching them: `git ls-remote`.

members.name: log
members.doc: Show history: `git log`.

members.name: logEntries
members.doc:
History as parsed {@link GitCommitEntry} values — SHA, parents, author,
dates, subject, and body — for building a changelog or deciding what a
range contains.

The lambda configures the walk (`.range()`, `.maxCount()`, `.paths()`);
the `--format` is fixed, since the parse depends on it.

members.name: show
members.doc: Show an object: `git show`.

members.name: diff
members.doc: Show changes: `git diff`.

members.name: diffNames
members.doc:
The changed paths of a diff, from `git diff --name-only -z`. What a target
needs to decide whether the work it guards has to run at all.

members.name: lsFiles
members.doc: List index and working-tree files: `git ls-files`.

members.name: lsFileNames
members.doc:
The paths of a `git ls-files -z` listing — git's own file list, ignore
rules already applied.

members.name: revParse
members.doc: Resolve revisions and repository paths: `git rev-parse`.

members.name: revision
members.doc:
A `git rev-parse` result as a trimmed string — the commit SHA, ref name,
or path a version stamp or cache key is built from.

members.name: describe
members.doc: Name a commit after the nearest tag: `git describe`.

members.name: merge
members.doc: Join two histories: `git merge`.

members.name: rebase
members.doc: Replay commits onto another base: `git rebase`.

members.name: cherryPick
members.doc: Apply existing commits here: `git cherry-pick`.

members.name: revert
members.doc: Undo commits with new ones: `git revert`.

members.name: reset
members.doc: Move the branch, index, and optionally the working tree: `git reset`.

members.name: stash
members.doc: Park and restore uncommitted work: `git stash`.

members.name: config
members.doc: Read or write configuration: `git config`.

members.name: configGet
members.doc:
One configuration value, or `undefined` when the key is unset — which
`git config --get` reports as a non-zero exit rather than as empty output.
The lambda must pick the key with `.get(...)` or `.getAll(...)`.

members.name: submodule
members.doc: Manage submodules: `git submodule add|init|update|sync|status|foreach`.

members.name: archive
members.doc: Package a tree as a tarball or zip: `git archive`.

members.name: apply
members.doc: Apply a patch file: `git apply`.

members.name: worktree
members.doc:
Manage worktrees: `git worktree add|list|remove|prune`. Pick the
subcommand in the lambda — `s.add(path)`, `s.list()`, `s.remove(path)`, or
`s.prune()`. For a listing to read rather than print, use
{@link GitTasksApi.worktreeList}.

members.name: worktreeList
members.doc:
List the repository's worktrees as parsed {@link GitWorktree} entries,
from `git worktree list --porcelain`.

The lambda configures the global options (`.dir()`, `.config()`); the
subcommand itself is fixed, since the parse depends on it.

members.name: defaultBranch
members.doc:
The name of a remote's default branch — `main`, `master`, or whatever it
chose — so a build does not have to hardcode one.

Reads the local `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD` first, which costs no network,
and asks the remote itself when that ref was never populated. Fails when
neither names a branch, rather than guessing.

members.name: mergeBase
members.doc: Find the common ancestor of commits: `git merge-base`.

members.name: isAncestor
members.doc:
Whether the first commit is an ancestor of the second:
`git merge-base --is-ancestor`, read back from its exit status.

members.name: revList
members.doc: Walk history as a list of commits: `git rev-list`.

members.name: commitCount
members.doc: How many commits the walk holds: `git rev-list --count`.

members.name: forEachRef
members.doc: List refs with a format: `git for-each-ref`.

members.name: refs
members.doc: The refs and what they point at, parsed: `git for-each-ref`.

members.name: showRef
members.doc: List or verify local refs: `git show-ref`.

members.name: symbolicRef
members.doc: Read or set a symbolic ref: `git symbolic-ref`.

members.name: nameRev
members.doc: Find symbolic names for commits: `git name-rev`.

members.name: lsTree
members.doc: List the contents of a tree: `git ls-tree`.

members.name: treeEntries
members.doc: The entries of a tree, parsed: `git ls-tree -z`.

members.name: catFile
members.doc: Read an object's contents or attributes: `git cat-file`.

members.name: blobText
members.doc: An object's contents as text, untrimmed: `git cat-file -p`.

members.name: checkIgnore
members.doc: Report which paths the ignore rules exclude: `git check-ignore`.

members.name: isIgnored
members.doc:
Whether a path is excluded, read from the exit status of
`git check-ignore`.

members.name: blame
members.doc: Annotate a file's lines with their commits: `git blame`.

members.name: blameLines
members.doc: The annotated lines, parsed: `git blame --porcelain`.

members.name: shortlog
members.doc: Summarise commits by contributor: `git shortlog`.

members.name: shortlogEntries
members.doc: The per-contributor commit counts, parsed: `git shortlog -s`.

members.name: grep
members.doc: Search tracked content: `git grep`.

members.name: verifyCommit
members.doc: Check a commit's signature: `git verify-commit`.

members.name: verifyTag
members.doc: Check a tag's signature: `git verify-tag`.

members.name: isSignatureValid
members.doc: Whether a commit's signature is good: `git verify-commit`.

members.name: isTagSignatureValid
members.doc: Whether a tag's signature is good: `git verify-tag`.

members.name: mergeTree
members.doc:
Merge in memory, leaving the index and working tree alone:
`git merge-tree`.

members.name: mergesCleanly
members.doc: Whether two commits merge without conflict: `git merge-tree`.

members.name: run
members.doc: Run any other git command via `.command(...)`.

symbols.name: GitTreeEntry
symbols.doc: One entry of `git ls-tree`: an object in a tree, and how it is recorded.

members.name: mode
members.doc: The file mode, e.g. `100644` for a regular file or `040000` for a tree.

members.name: type
members.doc: The kind of object: `blob`, `tree`, or `commit` for a submodule.

members.name: objectName
members.doc: The object name.

members.name: path
members.doc: The path, relative to the tree that was listed.

symbols.name: GitVerifyCommitSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `git verify-commit`.

members.name: verbose
members.doc: Also print the commit's contents (`-v`).

members.name: raw
members.doc: Print gpg's raw status output (`--raw`).

members.name: objects
members.doc: The commits to verify (positional); repeatable.

symbols.name: GitVerifyTagSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `git verify-tag`.

members.name: verbose
members.doc: Also print the tag's contents (`-v`).

members.name: raw
members.doc: Print gpg's raw status output (`--raw`).

members.name: format
members.doc:
The output format (`--format=<format>`), in git's placeholder language.
`verify-tag` accepts this where `verify-commit` does not.

members.name: objects
members.doc: The tags to verify (positional); repeatable.

symbols.name: GitWorktree
symbols.doc: One entry of `git worktree list --porcelain`.

members.doc:

symbols.name: LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT

commit message can contain, unlike the newlines a line-oriented format would
rely on.

symbols.name: REF_ENTRY_FORMAT
symbols.doc:
The `--format` {@link "./git.ts".GitTasks.refs} pins: the fields of one ref,
separated by NUL and terminated by one, so a ref name cannot break a record.

`%00` is git's own NUL placeholder, which is why the reader can rely on the
separator surviving a ref name containing anything else.

symbols.name: assertRefName
symbols.doc:
Reject a branch or tag name that git itself would.

Not cosmetic. These names are interpolated into request paths, and URL
normalisation resolves `..` before the request is sent — so
`../../../user/repos` as a branch turns `/repos/o/n/git/ref/heads/<branch>`
into `/repos/o/n/user/repos`, sending a write-scoped token somewhere the
caller never named. Validating here rather than trusting every caller is the
difference between an API that is safe to hand a string and one that is safe
only when used carefully.

The rules are git's own (see `git check-ref-format`), minus those that only
matter for multi-level refs.

symbols.name: CorrelateMode

- `"created-window"` — claim the `workflow_dispatch` run on the dispatch ref
  created just after dispatch; **best-effort**, for workflows that can't echo
  the marker (fails loudly if two candidates are in the window).

members.name: permission
members.doc:
Request one permission, e.g. `.permission("contents", "write")`. Repeatable.
Narrowing to what the target needs beats inheriting the app's full set;
requesting more than the installation grants is an error from GitHub.

The API names multi-word permissions with underscores (`pull_requests`), so
a hyphen is normalised to one. That spelling is the trap here:
`create-github-app-token` takes its inputs as `permission-pull-requests`,
and passing that form straight through is rejected as a permission the
installation does not grant — which reads as a misconfigured app rather
than a misspelled key.

members.name: checkRun
members.doc:
Post a completed check run for `.headSha(...)` named `.name(...)`, updating
the one already on that commit if there is one.

The lookup and the write are two calls, so this is an upsert by
convergence, not an atomic one: two callers racing on a commit that has no
check run yet can both find nothing and both create one. What it removes is
the *serial* duplicate — the retry, the re-drive, the supervisor finishing
a dead process's work — which is the case that actually happens.

Worth reporting rather than hiding: a caller that expected to create and
updated instead has learned that something else posted first, which is the
difference between a first attempt and a re-drive.

members.name: commit
members.doc:
Commit files through the API, with no git credential on disk.

Commits onto `.branch(...)`, or creates it from `.from(...)` when that is
set. The ref update is not forced, so a commit landing between reading the
head and writing it is rejected rather than silently overwritten — unless
`.replace()` is set, which resets an existing branch onto its base and
discards whatever was on it.

symbols.name: GhCommitSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for committing files through the API.

`owner/repo` and the token fall back to the Actions environment, so a job
that already has them needs to name only what it is committing.

members.doc: Add a file to the commit, replacing any earlier one at the same path.

members.name: branch
members.doc: The branch to commit onto. It must exist unless {@link from} is set.

members.name: from
members.doc:
Create {@link branch} from this one rather than committing onto an
existing branch. Creating a ref and moving one are different calls, and
which is wanted is the caller's to say rather than something to infer.

members.name: replace
members.doc:
Reset {@link branch} onto {@link from} when it already exists, rather than
failing because it does.

For a branch only one automated caller ever writes, and whose contents are
regenerated in full each time. Without this, a job that creates the branch
and then fails before opening its pull request can never retry: the second
run is refused because the ref it wants to create is already there, and the
work is stuck until someone deletes the branch by hand.

Deliberately not the default. Discarding commits on a branch that already
exists is exactly what should not happen to a branch someone is working on,
so it stays something the caller asks for.

symbols.doc: The pull-request operation {@link GhTasks} exposes.

members.name: pullRequest
members.doc:
Open a pull request from `.head(...)` onto `.base(...)`, or return the one
already open for that branch.

Idempotent on purpose. An unattended job that proposes the same branch
twice — because a later step failed and the whole thing ran again — should
find its existing proposal rather than fail on it.

An existing pull request is returned as it stands: the title and body set
here are not written over it, since the caller asked for a proposal to
exist and one does. `created` says which happened.

members.name: findPullRequest
members.doc:
Find the open pull request from `.head(...)` onto `.base(...)`, without
opening one.

For a caller that must know whether a proposal already exists *before* it
writes anything — because the answer changes what it should do, not just
what it should report. Opening one to find out is not a substitute: by
then the branch it would have to prepare has already been written.

members.name: uploadReleaseAsset
members.doc:
Attach a file to a GitHub release — the latest release by default, or the
one named by `.tag(...)`. Idempotent: an asset the release already
carries under the same name is kept as-is (unless `.refresh()` asks for
one with different bytes to be replaced), and a repository with no
releases resolves to `state: "no-release"` rather than throwing. Needs a
token with `contents: write`.

members.name: state
members.doc:
`uploaded` when the asset was sent; `refreshed` when `.refresh()` found
the release carrying different bytes under the name and replaced them;
`already-exists` when the release carries an asset of the same name that
was kept (nothing was changed); `no-release` when the repository has no
release to attach to.

members.doc:
The asset's `content-type`. Defaults by extension (`.tar.gz`/`.tgz`,
`.zip`, `.json`), then to `application/octet-stream`.

members.doc: The `owner/repo` to upload to. Defaults to `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`.

members.name: tag

members.name: refresh
members.doc:
Replace an asset the release already carries when its bytes differ from
the file's — compared by the sha256 digest the API reports — instead of
keeping it. An asset whose digest matches, or whose digest the API does
not report, is still kept: without a comparison to trust, replacement
would churn a published release's assets on every run, which is exactly
what the default protects. For an asset that must track its source
across runs (an extension archive, a docs bundle) on a long-lived
release.

members.doc:
The token to authenticate with — needs `contents: write`. Defaults to
`GITHUB_TOKEN` in the environment, so it never has to reach argv.

symbols.name: GhReleaseLatestApi
symbols.doc: The mark-latest operation {@link GhTasks} exposes.

members.name: markReleaseLatest
members.doc:
Point the repository's "Latest release" at the release for `.tag(...)`.

Idempotent, and quiet about it: a pointer already on the tag's release is
left untouched rather than re-written, so an unattended pipeline can run
this unconditionally without churning the release's audit history. A tag
with no release resolves to `state: "no-release"` rather than throwing —
the release may be cut by a later, human step — while a tag that does not
exist at all is an error, because the caller named it. Needs a token with
`contents: write`.

suspends the run until it finishes, and records its per-job conclusions to the
awaiting target's state (read them with {@link readWorkflowResult}). See the
module docs for the `run-name` correlation requirement and auth.

```ts
githubWorkflow((g) => g.repo("acme/app").workflow("e2e.yml").ref("main"))
```

symbols.name: GithubWorkflowSettings
symbols.doc:
Configuration for {@link githubWorkflow}, set through a settings lambda. Every
setter returns `this` so calls chain; `repo` and `workflow` are required.

members.name: repo
members.doc: Set the `OWNER/REPO` the workflow lives in.

members.name: workflow
members.doc: Set the workflow file name (e.g. `e2e.yml`) or numeric id.

members.name: ref
members.doc: Set the git ref to dispatch against (default `main`).

members.name: input
members.doc: Add one `workflow_dispatch` input.

members.name: inputs
members.doc: Merge a map of `workflow_dispatch` inputs.

members.name: markerInput
members.doc: Change the input name the correlation marker is dispatched as.

members.name: correlate
members.doc:
How the dispatched run is correlated: `"marker"` (default) matches the
marker echoed into the run's `run-name:`; `"created-window"` claims the
`workflow_dispatch` run on the dispatch ref created just after dispatch —
a **best-effort** fallback for a workflow that cannot echo the marker.

members.name: discoveryTimeout
members.doc:
How long after dispatch to keep looking for the run before failing fast with
guidance (a duration string; default one minute). Bounds the "workflow never
echoed the marker" failure so it surfaces in ~a minute instead of eating the
whole `.timeout()`.

members.name: pollEvery
members.doc: Set how often `zuke resume --check` should re-poll (a duration string).

members.name: repo_
members.doc: The `OWNER/REPO` slug the workflow lives in.

members.name: workflow_
members.doc: The workflow file name (e.g. `e2e.yml`) or its numeric id.

members.name: ref_
members.doc: The git ref to dispatch against (default `main`).

members.name: inputs_
members.doc: Extra `workflow_dispatch` inputs.

members.name: markerInput_
members.doc: The input name the marker is passed as (default `zuke_marker`).

members.name: correlateMode_
members.doc: How the dispatched run is correlated (default `"marker"`); set by {@link correlate}.

members.name: discoveryTimeoutMs_
members.doc: How long to wait for the run to appear before failing fast (ms); set by {@link discoveryTimeout}.

members.name: pollIntervalMs_
members.doc: Poll interval hint (ms) for `zuke resume --check`.

symbols.name: WorkflowCorrelationError
symbols.doc:
A {@link githubWorkflow} correlation failure the wait must **not** swallow as a
transient blip: the dispatched run could not be identified (it never echoed the
marker within the discovery window, or created-window correlation found more
than one candidate). Thrown from the trigger so the waiting target fails with
guidance instead of eating the whole `.timeout()`.

symbols.name: GitleaksDetectSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for [`gitleaks detect`](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks), which
scans a directory (and, by default, git history) for committed secrets.

members.name: source
members.doc: Path to scan (`--source`).

members.name: config
members.doc: Use an explicit gitleaks config (`--config`).

members.name: reportFormat
members.doc: Report format (`--report-format`), e.g. `json`, `sarif`, `csv`.

members.name: reportPath
members.doc: Write the report to a file (`--report-path`).

members.name: redact
members.doc: Redact secret values from the output (`--redact`).

members.name: noGit
members.doc: Treat the source as a plain directory, not a git repo (`--no-git`).

members.name: verbose
members.doc: Verbose output (`--verbose`).

members.name: logOpts
members.doc:
Restrict which commits are scanned, passed straight through to `git log`
(`--log-opts`).

Without this, `gitleaks detect` walks the whole history reachable from the
refs present in the checkout — so on a pull request, where CI typically
fetches every branch, a secret-shaped string on an unrelated branch fails
the scan and the failure appears on whichever pull request is looked at.
Passing a range such as `origin/main..HEAD` scopes the scan to the commits
under review.

Has no effect alongside {@linkcode noGit}, which makes gitleaks treat the
source as a plain directory and ignore history entirely.

symbols.name: AgentContext
symbols.doc: The failure context handed to an {@link AgentRunner}, plus a ready prompt.

members.name: target
members.doc: The name of the failed target.

members.name: attempt
members.doc: The 1-based recovery attempt.

members.name: command
members.doc: The command line that failed, if known.

members.name: output
members.doc: The captured error output (stderr, or the error message).

members.name: conventions
members.doc: Project conventions (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md), if found.

members.name: prompt
members.doc: A ready-to-use prompt assembled from the fields above.

symbols.name: agentFixer
symbols.doc:
Construct an {@link AgentFixer} from an {@link AgentRunner} and apply the
configuration lambda. Plug the result into a target with `.recoverWith(...)`.
symbols.signature: function agentFixer(run: AgentRunner, configure?: Configure<AgentFixer>): AgentFixer

symbols.name: AgentFixer
symbols.doc:
A fluent agent fixer. Construct one via {@link agentFixer} with a runner, and
attach it to a target with `.recoverWith(...)`. Diagnose/report defaults are
on; file changes happen through the agent, gated to local runs unless
`.runOnly(...)` says otherwise.

members.name: runOnly
members.doc:
Where the agent may run. Defaults to `"local"` — run on a developer's
machine, refuse on CI.

`"ci"` is the inverse, and the shape a repository's own build wants: an
agent that heals a pull request must not be turned loose on a working tree
someone is in the middle of editing. Off CI the fixer then reports the skip
and leaves the failure standing, without ever starting the agent.

`"both"` permits either host. One setter on one axis, so the effective
scope never depends on the order two flags were called in.

members.name: allowCI
members.doc: Permit the agent to run (and edit files) on CI as well as locally.

members.name: suggest
members.doc:
Propose the agent's changes as **committable inline `suggestion`s** on the
pull request (from its `git diff`) instead of committing them. The build
stays failed — the human applies the suggestions to fix it. Mutually
exclusive with {@link commitFixes} (suggest takes precedence). GitHub only;
elsewhere it falls back to the overview comment.

members.name: commitFixes
members.doc:
After the agent runs, stage all its changes, commit, and push to the current
branch so a healed PR carries the fix. Requires a checkout that can push; a
failed push is reported, not fatal.

members.name: commitMessage
members.doc: Override the commit subject used by {@link commitFixes}.

members.name: noPush
members.doc: Commit the fix but do not push it.

members.name: comment
members.doc: Also post what the agent did as a PR comment (on by default).

members.name: noComment
members.doc: Do not post a PR comment (the job summary is still written).

members.name: commentToken
members.doc: The token used to post the PR comment (defaults to the host's env var).

members.name: criteria
members.doc: Project-specific notes appended to the agent's prompt.

members.name: conventions
members.doc:
Supply the project conventions text directly instead of reading
`CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`. Pass an empty string to send none.

members.name: quiet
members.doc: Suppress the console printout (the summary/comment are still written).

members.name: env
members.doc: The environment reader used to detect CI and the comment host (test seam).

members.name: exec
members.doc: The `git` runner used for committing (test seam).

members.name: readFile
members.doc: The convention-file reader (test seam).

members.name: fetch
members.doc: The `fetch` implementation used to post the PR comment (test seam).

members.name: remediate
members.doc:
Run the agent against the failure, optionally commit its changes, and ask
the executor to re-run the target as the verifier. Skips (no retry)
outside the hosts {@link runOnly} permits, or if the agent run itself
fails.

members.name: name
members.doc: A name for diagnostics — `"agent fix"`.

symbols.name: AgentResult
symbols.doc:
What an {@link AgentRunner} may resolve to: a {@link CommandOutput} (its
stdout is captured for the report), a string, or nothing.

symbols.name: AgentRunner
symbols.doc:
Runs the coding agent against the assembled {@link AgentContext}. The agent is
expected to edit files in place; the executor then re-runs the target. Throw
(or let the underlying command throw) to signal the agent could not run.

symbols.name: aiCache
symbols.doc:
Construct an {@link AiCache}, applying an optional configure lambda so it can
be set up inline — e.g. `aiCache((c) => c.dir(".cache").ttl(3600))`.

symbols.name: AiCache
symbols.doc:
A best-effort cache of AI provider responses, keyed by a {@link stableHash} of
each call's salient parts and persisted through a {@link CacheStore} (the
default writes JSON files under {@link AiCache.dir}). Configure it inline with
{@link aiCache}: set the {@link AiCache.dir}, the {@link AiCache.ttl}, or
{@link AiCache.disable} it entirely, then read with {@link AiCache.get_} and
write with {@link AiCache.put_}.

members.name: dir
members.doc: Directory for the default file store (default ".zuke/ai-cache").

members.name: ttl
members.doc: Entries older than this many seconds are ignored (default 604800 = 7 days; 0 = never expire).

members.name: disable
members.doc: Turn the cache off programmatically ({@link get_} misses, {@link put_} is a no-op).

members.name: store
members.doc: Inject a custom backing store (test seam; overrides the file store).

members.name: now
members.doc: Clock seam for `createdAt` and TTL checks (default `Date.now`).

members.name: enabled_
members.doc: INTERNAL: whether the cache is active.

members.name: key_
members.doc: INTERNAL: derive a stable key from the given parts.

members.name: get_
members.doc: INTERNAL: fetch a live (non-expired) entry, or `undefined`.

members.name: put_
members.signature: put_(key: string, text: string, usage?: Usage): Promise<void>
members.doc: INTERNAL: store a response under `key`.

symbols.name: aiFixer
symbols.doc:
Construct an {@link AiFixer} and apply the configuration lambda. Plug the
result into a target with `.recoverWith(...)`:

```ts
test = target()
  .executes(() => DenoTasks.test((s) => s.allowAll()))
  .recoverWith(aiFixer((f) => f.provider("claude").apiKey(this.key)));
```

symbols.name: AiFixer
symbols.doc:
A fluent AI fixer. Construct one via {@link aiFixer}, configure it, and attach
it to a target with `.recoverWith(...)`. Only `.provider(...)` and
`.apiKey(...)` are required; everything else defaults.

members.name: provider
members.doc: Set the model provider (required).

members.name: apiKey
members.doc: Set the API key, from a secret parameter or a literal string (required).

members.name: model
members.doc: Override the model (default: the provider's recommended model).

members.name: effort
members.doc: Set the thinking-effort hint (honoured by Claude; ignored elsewhere).

members.name: criteria
members.doc: Project-specific notes appended to the prompt (idioms, constraints).

members.name: conventions
members.doc:
Supply the project conventions text directly, instead of letting the fixer
read `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`. Pass an empty string to send none.

members.name: diff
members.doc: Configure the diff source used for context (default: the working tree).

members.name: include
members.doc: Only include diff sections matching these globs in the prompt context.

members.name: exclude
members.doc: Exclude diff sections matching these globs from the prompt context.

members.name: maxDiffTokens
members.doc: Cap the context diff at roughly this many tokens (default 16000).

members.name: autoApply
members.doc:
Apply the proposed fix to the working tree and ask the executor to re-run
the target. Off by default (the fixer only diagnoses). Writes are confined
by {@link allowPaths}, the built-in exclusions, and {@link maxEdits}, and
are confined to the hosts {@link runOnly} permits.

members.name: allowPaths
members.doc: Restrict applied edits to paths matching these globs (default: all).

members.name: excludePaths
members.doc: Exclude paths matching these globs from edits, on top of the built-ins.

members.name: maxEdits
members.doc: Cap how many files a single applied fix may touch (default 10).

members.name: runOnly
members.doc:
Where the fixer may run. Defaults to `"local"` — apply on a developer's
machine, refuse on CI.

`"ci"` is the inverse, and the shape a repository's own build wants:
self-heal a pull request without ever rewriting a working tree someone is
in the middle of editing. Off CI the fixer then returns before the model is
called, so it costs no tokens and the underlying failure stands unchanged.

That is a stronger refusal than the default scope makes on CI, where the
fixer still diagnoses and only declines to write: a diagnosis on a pull
request is worth reading, whereas one on a local run is an unasked-for
charge against the developer's own key.

`"both"` permits either host. One setter on one axis, so the effective
scope never depends on the order two flags were called in.

```ts
aiFixer((f) => f.provider("openai").apiKey(key).autoApply().runOnly("ci"));
```

members.name: allowCI
members.doc: Permit auto-apply (and committing) on CI as well as locally.

members.name: commitFixes
members.doc:
After applying a fix, stage it, commit it, and push to the current branch —
so a healed pull request carries the fix as a commit. Implies
{@link autoApply}. Requires a checkout that can push (a non-detached branch
with credentials); a failed push is reported, not fatal.

members.name: commitMessage
members.doc: Override the commit subject used by {@link commitFixes}.

members.name: noPush
members.doc: Commit the fix but do not push it (leave it staged in a local commit).

members.name: comment
members.doc: Also post the diagnosis/fix as a PR comment (on by default).

members.name: noComment
members.doc: Do not post a PR comment (the job summary is still written).

members.name: suggest
members.doc:
On GitHub, post each code location as an inline review comment with a
committable `suggestion` block (the Copilot-style suggestion) instead
of a single overview comment. On by default; a no-op off GitHub or when the
model reports no specific locations, where the overview comment is used.

members.name: noSuggest
members.doc: Post a single overview comment instead of inline GitHub suggestions.

members.name: commentToken
members.doc: The token used to post the PR comment (defaults to the host's env var).

members.name: retry
members.doc: Retry the provider call on transient failures (see {@link RetryOptions}).

members.name: quiet
members.doc: Suppress the console printout (the summary/comment are still written).

members.name: fetch
members.doc: The `fetch` implementation for the API call (test seam).

members.name: exec
members.doc: The `git` runner used for the diff and commit (test seam).

members.name: write
members.doc: The file writer used when applying edits (test seam).

members.name: readFile
members.doc: The convention-file reader (test seam).

members.name: env
members.doc: The environment reader used to detect CI and the comment host (test seam).

members.name: budget
members.doc:
Attach a shared {@link Budget} that caps spend by an exact **token** count
(a USD cap is opt-in, computed from prices you supply to the budget). Once
the cap is reached the fixer skips the model call (and reports it) rather
than running up the bill; share one budget across reviewers and fixers to
bound a whole build.

members.name: cache
members.doc:
Reuse a prior fix for an identical failure (same provider, model, and
prompt) instead of calling the API again — see {@link AiCache}. Helpful when
the same failure recurs across CI re-runs; a hit does not draw down the
{@link budget}.

members.name: remediate
members.doc:
Diagnose the failure and, when permitted, apply (and commit) the fix. Always
reports; returns `{ retry: true }` only when it changed the working tree so
the executor re-runs the target as the verifier.

members.name: name
members.doc: A name for diagnostics — `"AI fix"`.

symbols.name: AiReviewError
symbols.doc: Raised when a reviewer is misconfigured, the API fails, or the gate trips.

members.name: name
members.doc: The error name.

symbols.name: aiReviewWorkflow
AiReviewWorkflowSpec
symbols.doc: What to generate — only `reviewers` is required.

members.name: reviewers
members.doc:
The reviewers whose key env vars and `.comment()` setting drive the
generated workflow. Each reviewer's `.apiKey(param)` parameter becomes an
`env:` entry (or its host equivalent) that maps the secret in; any
reviewer with `.comment()` causes the workflow to grant the right
commenting scope and pass the host's token env var.

members.name: host
members.doc:
The CI host the workflow targets. Defaults to `"github"`. Use `"gitlab"`,
`"azure"`, or `"bitbucket"` to generate the equivalent for those hosts.

members.name: target
members.doc: The build target the workflow runs. Defaults to `"review"`.

members.name: baseBranch
members.doc:
The base branch the diff is taken against (used by the GitHub workflow's
fetch step). Defaults to `"master"`.

members.name: fetchBase
members.doc:
Emit the `git fetch` step that makes the base branch available, and point
the reviewers at what it fetched. Defaults to `true`, because a pull-request
checkout is shallow and has no base to diff against.

Set it to `false` when the build's review target fetches its own base — then
the workflow drops the step, and the reviewers use their own configured base
rather than the fetched `FETCH_HEAD`. Preferable where it applies: the same
`zuke review` then works locally, where no workflow step exists to run.

members.name: hardenRunner
members.doc:
The pinned `step-security/harden-runner@<sha>` to harden the runner with.

Supplying this — or {@link checkout} — renders the two separate steps
instead of the prelude action, because naming an action means those
specific actions were asked for. Leave both unset for the default, which
is the one action that does both and carries its own pin.

members.name: checkout
members.doc:
The pinned `actions/checkout@<sha>` to check the repository out with.
Like {@link hardenRunner}, supplying it renders the separate steps.

members.name: pins
members.doc:
Resolves each action's pinned reference by name, exactly as `cicd`'s own
option does.

Supply it when the build sources pins from somewhere that stays current.
Without it the prelude action falls back to the reference baked into the
core this package resolved against — which is a release behind as soon as
the action is released again, and silently so: this file would name a
different commit from every other generated workflow in the repository,
and only a diff would show it.

members.name: path
members.doc: Output path. Defaults to the host's conventional location.

members.name: name
members.doc: Workflow name shown in the host's UI. Defaults to `"AI Review"`.

members.name: timeoutMinutes
members.doc: Per-job timeout in minutes. Defaults to 15.

symbols.name: Assessment
symbols.doc: The structured result of a review.

members.name: score
members.doc: Overall risk score, `0` (none) to `10` (severe).

members.name: severity
members.doc: The overall severity.

members.name: summary
members.doc: A one-line summary of the assessment.

members.name: findings
members.doc: The individual findings.

symbols.name: AssessmentFinding
symbols.doc: A single issue reported by the model.

members.name: title
members.doc: A short title for the issue.

members.name: severity
members.doc: The issue's severity.

members.name: id
members.doc:
A stable fingerprint for the finding, assigned by the reviewer (see
{@link "./suppress.ts".findingFingerprint}). Copy it into the suppress
list to dismiss a recurring false positive.

members.name: file
members.doc: The file the issue is in, if the model attributed one.

members.name: line
members.doc: The line the issue is at, if the model attributed one.

members.name: detail
members.doc: A longer explanation, if provided.

members.name: verification
members.doc:
The verify pass's verdict on this finding, when `.verify()` ran and the
verifier answered for it: `"confirmed"` means the concrete failure path
was traced, `"uncertain"` means the evidence neither confirmed nor refuted
it. Both stay reported and gate — only a refutation (which removes the
finding and lists it in the report's refuted table) mutes a candidate.
Absent when verify did not run or returned no verdict for the finding.

symbols.name: AssessmentType
symbols.doc: The kind of review an assessment performs.
symbols.signature: type AssessmentType = generic | security | secrets | correctness | license

symbols.name: budget
symbols.doc:
Construct a {@link Budget}, applying an optional configure lambda so caps can
be set inline — e.g. `budget((b) => b.maxTokens(100_000).maxCost(1))`.

symbols.name: Budget
symbols.doc:
A running token and cost budget for AI provider calls. Build one with
{@link budget}, set caps with the fluent setters, then fold each call's usage
in with {@link Budget.record_} and gate further calls on
{@link Budget.exhausted_}.

members.name: maxTokens
members.doc: Cap total tokens (input + output across all recorded calls).

members.name: maxCost
members.doc:
Cap estimated USD cost. Only takes effect for models you've priced via
{@link prices} — no prices ship by default — so the estimate uses your own
current rates. Pair it with {@link maxTokens} for a guaranteed hard cap.

members.name: prices
members.doc:
Supply per-model prices (USD per 1,000,000 tokens, keyed by model id) so a
{@link maxCost} cap and the cost estimate can be computed. Merges across
calls. Nothing is priced until you call this — provider pricing changes too
often to bake a table in, so the rates here are yours to keep current.

members.name: exhausted_
members.doc: INTERNAL: whether a configured cap has already been reached.

members.name: record_
members.signature: record_(usage: Usage | undefined, model: string): void
members.doc: INTERNAL: fold one provider call's usage into the running totals.

members.name: spend_
members.doc: INTERNAL: a snapshot of consumption so far.

members.name: remainingTokens_
members.doc: INTERNAL: remaining tokens before the cap, or undefined when no token cap.

members.name: describe_
members.doc: INTERNAL: a one-line human summary, e.g. "1,234 tokens (~$0.01) of 10,000 / $1.00".

symbols.name: BudgetSpend
symbols.doc: A snapshot of what a {@link Budget} has consumed so far.

members.name: calls
members.doc: How many provider calls were recorded.

members.name: inputTokens
members.doc: Total input (prompt) tokens across all recorded calls.

members.name: outputTokens
members.doc: Total output (completion) tokens across all recorded calls.

members.name: totalTokens
members.doc: Total tokens (input + output) across all recorded calls.

members.name: cost
members.doc: Estimated USD cost, when at least one recorded call had a known price.

symbols.name: CacheEntry
symbols.doc: A cached provider response.

members.name: text
members.doc: The model's raw text response.

members.name: usage
members.doc: Token usage reported for the original call, if any.

members.name: createdAt
members.doc: Epoch milliseconds when the entry was written (for TTL).

symbols.name: CacheStore
symbols.doc: A pluggable backing store for the cache (the default is file-backed).

members.name: get
members.doc: Fetch the entry stored under `key`, or `undefined` when absent.

members.name: set
members.doc: Store `entry` under `key`, replacing any prior value.

symbols.name: Confidence
symbols.doc: The model's confidence that a fix is correct.

symbols.name: correctnessReviewer
symbols.doc: A reviewer that scores the diff for correctness bugs and regressions.

symbols.name: DiffFetch
symbols.doc:
The base-branch fetch a {@link DiffSettings.fetchBase} requested — the remote
to fetch from and the branch (auto-detected from CI when unset).

members.name: branch
members.doc: The branch to fetch, or `undefined` to auto-detect it from the CI env.

members.name: remote
members.doc: The remote to fetch from (default `"origin"`).

symbols.name: DiffSettings
symbols.doc: Fluent diff source configuration passed to {@link "./reviewer.ts".Reviewer.diff}.

members.name: base
members.doc: Review the diff against `ref` (e.g. `"origin/main"`).

members.name: staged
members.doc: Review the staged changes (`git diff --cached`).

members.name: text
members.doc: Review a diff supplied directly, bypassing `git` (useful in tests).

members.name: fetchBase
members.doc:
Fetch the base branch (a shallow, tag-less `git fetch`) before diffing, and
diff against it — so CI needs no manual `git fetch` step. With no `branch`,
the base is auto-detected from the CI environment (GitHub's `GITHUB_BASE_REF`
— the pull request's base branch). Honoured by the {@link
"./fixer.ts".AiFixer}; if the fetch fails it falls back to the working-tree
diff.

members.name: text_

members.name: base_

members.name: fetch_

The base-branch fetch requested via {@link DiffSettings.fetchBase}, or
`undefined` when none was requested.

members.name: argv_

symbols.name: DiscussionSettings
symbols.doc:
Fluent settings for {@link "./reviewer.ts".Reviewer.discussion} — who the
reviewer listens to on the PR thread, and how much of it the model may see.

members.name: trustAssociations
members.doc:
Replace the trusted `author_association` set (default `OWNER`, `MEMBER`,
`COLLABORATOR`). Comments from authors outside it (and outside
{@link trustAuthors}) are dropped before the model sees them.

members.name: trustAuthors
members.doc:
Trust these author logins in addition to the association rule — e.g. an
outside collaborator whose review the project wants the reviewer to
engage with.

members.name: maxCommentTokens
members.doc:
Cap the total comment text sent to the model at roughly this many tokens
(default 4000), newest comments kept first — so a wall of text cannot
crowd the diff and the rubric out of the context window.

members.name: associations_
members.doc: INTERNAL: the trusted association set.

members.name: authors_
members.doc: INTERNAL: the extra trusted author logins.

members.name: threads
members.doc:
Also anchor each finding to a file/line **review thread** on the pull
request, so a maintainer contests it by replying in that thread instead of
quoting its id somewhere on the PR.

The summary comment is posted either way and stays the one source of
truth: it lists every finding — anchored or not — and carries the state
block, so a thread that cannot be posted never hides a finding. The
reviewer replies into the thread with the outcome and resolves it once the
finding is fixed or dismissed. GitHub only; on other hosts the reviewer
notes that and posts the summary alone.

members.name: maxTokens_
members.doc: INTERNAL: the total comment-token cap.

members.name: threads_
members.doc: INTERNAL: whether findings are also anchored to review threads.

symbols.name: Effort

symbols.signature: type Effort = low | medium | high | xhigh | max

symbols.name: EnvReader
symbols.doc: Read an environment variable, tolerating an absent `--allow-env` permission.

symbols.name: FileEdit

members.name: content

symbols.name: findingFingerprint
symbols.doc:
A stable fingerprint for a finding: hash of the assessment kind, the
normalised title (trimmed, lowercased, whitespace collapsed), and the file.
Independent of line number so a finding keeps its id as code shifts.
symbols.signature: function findingFingerprint(assessment: AssessmentType, finding: AssessmentFinding): string

members.name: rootCause

members.name: confidence
members.doc: The model's confidence that the edits resolve the failure.

members.name: locations
members.doc: The specific code locations the fix targets, with verbatim source.

members.name: edits

symbols.name: FixLocation
symbols.doc:
A specific code location the fix targets: the exact offending source quoted
verbatim, its file and line(s), and the suggested replacement. Rendered as a
diff in the report so the comment shows real code, not just prose.

members.name: file

members.name: line
members.doc: The 1-based line where the offending code starts.

members.name: endLine
members.doc: The 1-based line where it ends, when it spans more than one line.

members.name: code
members.doc: The exact offending source line(s), quoted verbatim.

members.name: suggestion
members.doc: The suggested replacement for {@link code} (empty means delete it).

symbols.name: GateRule
symbols.doc: A configured rule for {@link "./reviewer.ts".Reviewer.failWhen}.

symbols.name: GateSettings
symbols.doc: Fluent gate configuration passed to {@link "./reviewer.ts".Reviewer.failWhen}.

members.name: scoreAbove
members.doc: Fail when the assessed risk score is strictly above `value` (0–10).

members.name: severityAtLeast
members.doc: Fail when the overall severity is at least `value`.

members.name: rules_
members.doc: The configured gate rules, in the order they were added.

symbols.name: genericReviewer
symbols.doc:
A general-purpose reviewer scored on code quality and maintainability. Pair
with `.criteria(...)` to add project-specific notes (idioms, conventions, a
coding-style document); the built-in rubric is sufficient without them.

symbols.name: licenseReviewer
symbols.doc: A reviewer that scores the diff for license and compliance risk.

symbols.name: ModelPrice
symbols.doc: Per-model price in USD per 1,000,000 tokens.

members.name: output
members.doc: USD per 1,000,000 output (completion) tokens.

symbols.name: Provider
symbols.doc: A supported model provider.

symbols.name: RetryInfo
symbols.doc: What happened before a retry, for {@link RetryOptions.onRetry}.

members.name: attempt
members.doc: The attempt that just failed (1-based).

members.name: attempts
members.doc: The total number of attempts that will be made.

members.name: delayMs
members.doc: How long the helper will wait before the next attempt, in milliseconds.

members.name: reason
members.doc: Why the attempt failed — e.g. `"HTTP 503"` or `"timed out after 60000ms"`.

symbols.name: RetryOptions
symbols.doc: Configurable knobs for {@link retryingFetch}.

members.name: attempts
members.doc: Total attempts (first try + retries). Defaults to {@link DEFAULT_ATTEMPTS}.

members.name: baseDelayMs
members.doc: Backoff for the first retry; doubles each subsequent retry.

members.name: timeoutMs
members.doc: Per-attempt timeout in milliseconds (default 60s). `0` disables it.

members.name: onRetry
members.doc: Invoked before each retry, so a caller can report progress.

members.name: sleep
members.doc: Sleep seam — overridden in tests so retries don't take real time.

symbols.name: Reviewer
symbols.doc:
A fluent AI reviewer. Construct one via {@link securityReviewer} (and the
sibling factories), configure it, and attach it to a target with
`.validateBefore(...)` / `.validateAfter(...)`. `.provider(...)` and
`.apiKey(...)` are required; everything else has a default.

members.name: provider_
members.doc: The model provider, once `.provider(...)` has been called.

members.name: apiKey_
members.doc: The configured API key (a parameter — for its env var — or a literal).

members.name: commentEnabled_
members.doc: Whether `.comment()` is set — i.e. this reviewer posts to the PR.

members.name: commentToken_
members.doc: The configured comment-posting token, if `.commentToken(...)` was called.

members.name: provider
members.doc: Set the model provider (required).

members.name: apiKey
members.doc: Set the API key, from a secret parameter or a literal string (required).

members.name: model
members.doc: Override the model (default: the provider's recommended model).

members.name: effort
members.doc: Set the thinking-effort hint (honoured by Claude; ignored elsewhere).

members.name: criteria
members.doc:
Optional project-specific notes appended above the diff in the user prompt
— framing that fine-tunes the built-in rubric (e.g. "strict TypeScript,
no `any`/`as`"). Works for every reviewer; the assessment's own system
prompt already covers what to look for, so this is purely additive.

members.name: diff
members.doc: Configure the diff source (default: the working-tree diff, `git diff`).

members.name: include
members.doc: Only review files matching these globs (default: all files).

members.name: exclude
members.doc: Exclude files matching these globs (in addition to lockfiles).

members.name: maxDiffTokens
members.doc: Cap the diff at roughly this many tokens, truncating the rest.

members.name: failWhen
members.doc: Choose the gate that breaks the build (default: score above 7).

members.name: onError
members.doc:
What to do when the review itself fails (API error, refusal, bad JSON):
`"fail"` breaks the build (default), `"warn"` logs and passes.

members.name: retry
members.doc:
Retry the provider call on transient failures (`HTTP 408/429/500/502/503/
504` and network errors). The default is on — three attempts with
exponential backoff and `Retry-After` honoured. Pass an object to override:
`{ attempts: 5 }` to retry more, or `{ attempts: 1 }` to disable.

members.name: skipIfKeyMissing
members.doc:
Skip the review (instead of failing) when the API key is missing — handy
when the key is a CI-only secret. The skip is announced on the console and
in the job summary so the gap is visible.

members.name: comment
members.doc:
Also post the review to the pull/merge request as a comment. Works on
every supported CI host — GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure Pipelines,
Bitbucket Pipelines — dispatched at runtime by {@link detectCiHost}. A
no-op outside a PR context (e.g. local runs). On each host the workflow
must grant the right scope: GitHub `pull-requests: write`, GitLab a token
with the `api` scope, Azure `System.AccessToken`, Bitbucket an app
password.

`mode` chooses how re-runs post: `"update"` (default) keeps a single
comment per reviewer, edited in place; `"append"` posts a fresh comment
every run, so earlier assessments — and their finding ids — stay on the
thread as history. The discussion feature works with both: its state block
rides on every comment, and the newest one is read back.

members.name: commentToken
members.doc:
The token used to post the PR/MR comment. Defaults to the active host's
conventional env var: `GITHUB_TOKEN` (GitHub), `GITLAB_TOKEN` (GitLab),
`SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN` (Azure), `BITBUCKET_TOKEN` (Bitbucket).

members.name: githubToken
members.doc: Backwards-compatible alias for {@link commentToken}.

members.name: quiet
members.doc: Suppress the findings printout and the job-summary section.

members.name: fetch
members.doc: The `fetch` implementation for the API call (test seam).

members.name: exec
members.doc: The `git` runner used to produce the diff (test seam).

members.name: env
members.doc:
Environment reader used to auto-detect the base branch for
{@link "./diff.ts".DiffSettings.fetchBase} (reads `GITHUB_BASE_REF`). A test
seam; defaults to the process environment.

members.name: budget
members.doc:
Attach a shared {@link Budget} that caps spend by an exact **token** count
(a USD cap is opt-in, computed from prices you supply to the budget). Pass
the same budget to several reviewers and a fixer to bound the whole build:
once the cap is reached, further reviews are skipped (not failed) with a
note, rather than running up the bill.

members.name: cache
members.doc:
Reuse a prior model response for an identical review (same provider, model,
and prompt) instead of calling the API again — see {@link AiCache}. A cache
hit costs nothing and does not draw down the {@link budget}.

members.name: suppress
members.doc:
Hide findings whose stable ID is in a {@link Suppressions} list — a learned
set of dismissed false positives. Every finding is fingerprinted and its ID
surfaced in the report, so dismissing one is a copy-paste into the list.

members.name: conventionsFile
members.doc:
Feed the project's conventions document (e.g. `AGENTS.md`) to the model as
reference material, so the review judges the change against the project's
documented rules instead of generic taste. When the diff has a base ref
(`.diff((d) => d.base(...))` or a successful `.fetchBase()`), the file is
read from that **base** via `git show` — never from the head under review,
so a pull request cannot rewrite the rules it is judged by. Without a base
(a local working-tree review) it is read from disk. Truncated at roughly
`maxTokens` (default 8000).

members.name: fileContext
members.doc:
Also send the full post-image contents of the changed files (read via
`git show HEAD:<path>`), bounded at roughly `maxTokens` (default 12000) —
so the model can check a finding against the surrounding code (an existing
guard, a validation a few lines away) instead of judging hunks in
isolation. Skipped silently for a literal `.diff((d) => d.text(...))`
source with no repository behind it.

members.name: verify
members.doc:
Add an adversarial verification pass: after the review produces candidate
findings, a second model call re-checks each against the diff (and the
{@link fileContext}, when enabled) and refutes any whose failure path it
cannot concretely trace. Refuted candidates are listed in the report but
neither posted as findings nor gated on. Costs one extra API call per
review with findings; if the pass itself errors, the unverified findings
are kept (fail toward reporting, never toward silence).

members.name: discussion
members.doc:
Engage with the pull-request discussion instead of repeating findings: the
reviewer reads the PR's comments, and when a **trusted** commenter (by the
host's own author metadata — see {@link DiscussionSettings}) contests a
finding by quoting its ID, an adjudication pass weighs the rebuttal on
technical merit and either upholds the finding (with the gap named) or
dismisses it. Dismissals persist across runs in a state block inside the
reviewer's own PR comment, so a dismissed finding — or a rewording of it —
does not resurface without new evidence. Requires {@link comment} (the
comment is where state lives) and a host that can list comments (GitHub
currently); elsewhere the discussion is skipped with a console note.

Untrusted comments are dropped in code before any prompt is built — the
model never sees them, so a drive-by "the maintainer approved this"
comment cannot influence the review.

members.name: validate
members.doc:
Run the review and gate the build. Throws an {@link AiReviewError} when the
gate trips (or on a configuration/API error with `onError: "fail"`).

members.name: name
members.doc: A name for diagnostics — `"<assessment> review"`.

symbols.name: RunScope
symbols.doc:
Where a fixer may run, set with `.runOnly(...)`.

- `"local"` — apply on a developer's machine, refuse on CI. The default, and
  what a fixer has when `.runOnly(...)` is never called.
- `"ci"` — apply on CI, and do not run at all off it. The scope a
  repository's own build wants: heal a pull request without ever rewriting a
  working tree someone is editing.
- `"both"` — apply on either host. What `.allowCI()` selects.

"On CI" means a host `detectCiHost` recognises: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI,
Azure Pipelines and Bitbucket Pipelines. Anywhere else — CircleCI, Jenkins,
or a runner that only sets the generic `CI` variable — counts as local, so
`"ci"` does not run there and `"local"` does. That is the safe direction for
`"ci"` (an unrecognised host gets no writes rather than unexpected ones), but
it does mean a fixer scoped to `"ci"` on such a runner will report a skip
every time instead of fixing anything. Use `"both"` there.

symbols.name: secretsReviewer
symbols.doc: A reviewer that scans the diff for leaked secrets and credentials.

symbols.name: securityReviewer
symbols.doc: A reviewer that scores the diff for security vulnerabilities.

symbols.name: Severity
symbols.doc: A severity level, ordered `none` < `low` < `medium` < `high` < `critical`.
symbols.signature: type Severity = none | low | medium | high | critical

symbols.name: suppressions
symbols.doc:
Construct a {@link Suppressions}, applying an optional configure lambda so the
file and inline fingerprints can be set inline — e.g.
`suppressions((s) => s.file(".zuke/suppress.json").add("abc"))`.

symbols.name: Suppressions
symbols.doc:
A file-backed set of suppressed finding fingerprints. The effective set is
the union of the fingerprints read from {@link Suppressions.file} and any
added inline with {@link Suppressions.add}; the reviewer drops a finding whose
{@link findingFingerprint} is in that set.

members.name: file
members.doc: Path of the JSON suppress list (default ".zuke/ai-suppress.json").

members.name: add
members.doc: Add fingerprints inline (in addition to any from the file).

members.name: reader
members.doc: Reader seam for the suppress file (default reads from disk, missing -> undefined).

members.name: load_
members.doc: INTERNAL: the effective set of suppressed fingerprints (file ∪ inline).

symbols.name: Usage
symbols.doc:
Token counts a provider reported for a review call, when the response carries
them. Each field is optional because not every provider reports every count.

members.name: inputTokens
members.doc: Tokens in the prompt / input.

members.name: outputTokens
members.doc: Tokens in the model's output / completion.

members.name: totalTokens
members.doc: Total tokens, reported by the provider or derived from input + output.
